QUICK RETRIBUTION. A Murderer Lynched on the Night After His Deed Was Committed.
DEADWOOD, DAK., Aug. 27.—Dr. H. P. Lynch of Sturgis was shot dead Monday night in his office by Corporal Ross Hallis of Company A, Twenty-fifth United States Infantry, stationed at Fort Meade, and the latter was lynched Tuesday night by a mob. Some time ago Hallis beat a colored woman and broke three of her ribs. Dr. Lynch was called to attend her and was also summoned as a witness before the grand jury. Hallis was indicted and threatened to kill the doctor. The night of the murder he deserted the Fort, got a change of clothing, went to Sturgis, crept stealthily up to the doctor's office and fired at his victim through the window. The assassination was soon discovered, and Hallis was arrested for the crime. On being confronted with proof of his guilt he confessed. Tuesday night a mob seized him and hanged him. Dr. Lynch was very popular and was in great demand as a practitioner. He was 53 years old, and came to the hills from St. Genevieve, Mo., in 1876. His body was buried yesterday with Masonic honors.

Hanged by a Dakota Mob for Murdering a Doctor.

Hollis was indicted and threatened to kill the doctor. The night of the murder he deserted the fort, got a change of clothing, went to Sturgis, crept stealthily up to the doctor's office and fired at his victim through the window. The assassination was soon discovered, and Hollis was arrested for the crime yesterday. On being confronted with proofs of his guilt he confessed. Last night a mob seized him and hanged him.

DEADWOD DAY. August 98. Great excite.
THREATENING TO BURN THE TOWN WHERE CORPORAL HOLLIS WAS LYNCHED.
DEADWOOD, DAK., August 28.—Great excitement prevailed in Sturgis, the scene of the lynching of Ross Hollis, the colored soldier assassin of Dr. Lynch yesterday. A number of colored soldiers of Fort Meade, members of the 25th U. S. infantry, armed themselves and proceeded to the town of Sturgis, threatening to burn the place. Trouble seemed imminent, but Gen. Sturgis, commanding at Fort Meade, on being informed, detailed a patrol of the 7th cavalry which scoured the town, capturing and returning the disaffected men to the post immediately after the burial of Dr. Lynch.

TWO OF A KIND.
Lynchers of Dakota and Texas Get in Their Work.

Dapids City (Dak.) dispatch: Wednesday night Dr. Lynch, a physician practicing at Sturgis, was shot and killed by some unknown person. Suspicion attached to a negro named Corporal Hollis, of Company A, Twenty-fifth regiment, stationed at Ft. Meade, two miles from Sturgis. Yesterday he was arrested, confessed the crime, and about midnight last night he was taken just outside of town and lynched. It is said that Hollis had been keeping company with a wench, and not long since abused her shamefully, breaking three of her ribs. Dr. Lynch attended her and advised her to prosecute Hollis, as she was permanently injured by him. The doctor being the only witness against him, Hollis shot him to put him out of the way.

Information from San Marcos, Texas, reports that a mob of 75 persons at Blanco went to the jail and demanded of Sheriff Jackson the keys. Jackson did not have them and declared he could not procure them. After a struggle Jackson was overpowered and the keys found on his person. The mob entered the jail, took out Lockie, the man who committed the wholesale murder in Johnson City a few days ago, and hanged him after obtaining a statement in regard to his crimes. Lockie made a full confession and said he had intended to kill the members of three or four families besides those he murdered. He was prevented from doing so by his cartridges giving out.
